releases.body:
### Stop now closes the TUI terminal, including after a restart

* Pressing Stop on a card whose project had an open TUI terminal only marked the
  run `cancelled`; the window stayed open. Two defects: `/api/runs/{uid}/cancel`
  called `ProcessTracker.terminate()` only when the in-memory entry existed — after
  a server restart it does not — so the persisted `runs.pid` + `PERUN_RUN_UID`
  marker were never consulted; and the kill target was whatever the marker scan
  returned first, usually the *agent* process inside the terminal.
* The endpoint now always offers the run to the tracker (which no-ops to
  `finalize()` when nothing is attributable). `terminate()` resolves the **shell
  that owns the terminal** via `_terminal_owner()` — the outermost
  `cmd`/`pwsh`/`sh` carrying the marker in its command line — because `cmd /k` and
  `pwsh -NoExit` keep the window at a prompt after the agent exits. Liveness still
  follows the agent process, so an agent that exits still ends its run.
* Regression tests: the kill target is the shell, not its child; a stop after a
  restart kills the shell around the persisted agent pid; `/cancel` reaches the
  tracker with an empty in-memory map.

### Stop never guesses which process to kill

* `ProcessTracker.terminate()` now resolves its target through `_kill_pid()`: a
  pid carrying the run's `PERUN_RUN_UID` marker, or Perun's own live `Popen`
  handle. The launch-time Windows Terminal heuristic in `_resolve_child_pid()` is
  skipped on that path (`heuristic=False`) — it matches "a terminal window that
  appeared around launch time", and closing it could take down tabs belonging to
  other runs. It stays available for `is_alive()`, where it only decides liveness.
  With nothing attributable, Stop finalizes the row and reports `cancelled: false`
  instead of killing an unrelated process; `kill_all_explicit()` uses the same
  rule.
* Regression tests: a live Stop never asks the resolver for a heuristic match, an
  unattributable live pid survives a Stop while the run row is finalized, and the
  existing marker/restart cases still pass.
* `_watch_loop()` now guards each run's liveness/finalize step. A DB hiccup (a
  lock, a closed handle) used to raise inside the watcher thread and silently stop
  auto-finalization, which is the only thing that clears a run row when the user
  closes the terminal.
* Docs (AGENTS, CODEMAP, TECHNICAL) state the exact rule, so "Stop closes the TUI
  terminal" and "never kill a process Perun cannot attribute" are both true.
* Test/doc drift fixed: `tests/test_js_card_controls.py` no longer mentions the
  withdrawn Finish action, and its rename assertion matches what it checks.

### A working project card shows Stop again

* The card rendered **▶ Run** unconditionally and only *added* a Stop button for
  runs that were not standalone. Every TUI session opened from the dashboard is
  `standalone=1` for its whole life, so Stop was never rendered for it (since
  v0.10.3, when the restart-marker fix suppressed it) — an active card showed
  "working" plus a Run button that would have started a second session.
* `web/js/card_controls.js` (`runControlSpec`, unit-tested with `node --test`) now
  decides the first card action: **Run** when the project is idle, **Stop** for
  any active run. Stop calls `POST /api/runs/{uid}/cancel`, which is already the
  intended path — cancel a headless run, or close the terminal Perun opened for a
  TUI run (it only kills a pid carrying that run's `PERUN_RUN_UID` marker, and it
  still works after a restart from the persisted `runs.pid`).
* `applyCardStates()` re-syncs that control on every 4 s presence poll, so a card
  that lights up, is stopped or is swept swaps its button in place, and
  `openProjectTui()` swaps it immediately for the run it just started. The button
  is rebuilt only when its kind or run id actually changed.
* The card's `Run` tooltip and doc text now match what it does (OpenCode launched
  in the project directory, not the Agent Console).

### A working project card offers its run's control, never Run

* After a browser refresh, a card whose project had an active session showed a
  "working" pip and banner but still rendered **▶ Run**. A standalone TUI run had
  its Stop button suppressed ("Perun cannot stop it") while Run was hardcoded, so
  the card invited a second session next to the working one. The first card
  action now comes from `web/js/card_controls.js` (`runControlSpec`, unit-tested
  with `node --test`): **Run** when idle, **Stop** for a headless run Perun owns,
  **Finish** for a standalone TUI run — which calls
  `POST /api/runs/{uid}/finish`, marks it done and captures usage, and never kills
  the terminal.
* `applyCardStates()` re-syncs that control on every 4 s presence poll (so a card
  that lights up, finishes or is swept changes its action in place), and
  `openProjectTui()` swaps it immediately for the run it just started. The button
  is only rebuilt when its kind or run id actually changed.
* The card's `Run` no longer goes through the Agent Console: its tooltip and doc
  text now match what it does (OpenCode launched in the project directory).

### Usage cards refresh on their own

* The dashboard's **Usage · captured in the last 24h** card and the project
  page's usage line now re-fetch every 60 seconds while their view is open,
  instead of only on first render (a browser reload or a tab switch was the only
  way to see a run's new numbers). The timer stops itself when the view changes,
  is replaced on re-render, and never overlaps a request. 60 s matches the data:
  open TUI runs are captured every 5 minutes, headless runs at finalize.

### Audit follow-ups from the v0.10.44 review

* `tools/release.py` puts the checkout on `sys.path` before importing
  `perun.release_notes`, so bundling the notes no longer depends on
  `PYTHONPATH` or an installed copy (a failed import there would have left a
  half-prepared release).
* A test covers `GET /api/update/notes?version=<unknown>`: an unknown version
  reports `source: "unavailable"` and an empty body instead of inventing notes.
* The Shared tab says that hiding a project does not disable sharing — turn the
  toggle off to tear its room down.

### The self-update page shows what the installed release changed

* `GET /api/update/notes` returns the changelog section for the running version,
  and the Updates page renders it as **"What changed in vX.Y.Z"**. The Windows
  installer excludes `docs/`, so the release pipeline now bundles the last ten
  releases into `perun/release_notes.json`; a git checkout falls back to
  `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. When an update is available, the GitHub notes are shown
  separately as "What's new in vX" instead of replacing the installed summary.
* `tools/release.py` regenerates the bundle on every release, and a test fails if
  it is stale.

### The hidden control project can be shared on purpose, and is reconciled like any other

* `reconcile_all_project_chats()` now walks `list_projects(include_hidden=True)`.
  Hiding a project only keeps it out of lists; if the owner explicitly shares
  `perun` (`shared: true` plus participants on the `perunchat_trusted` list), its
  room is created, joined and repaired after a reconnect exactly like a normal
  shared project. Access is the participant list, not a special case, and HITL
  approval, the guard allowlist and the post-run audit are unchanged.
* Telegram remains optional: the CLI, TUI, dashboard (loopback + token) and MCP
  work without it. The MCP cwd rule from 0.10.43 still applies to local sessions
  (and does not affect a shared execution, which runs in the project directory).

### The control plane is reachable only from its own checkout

* The MCP project resolver now includes **hidden** projects when it matches the
  caller's working directory, so a session in the Perun checkout is scoped to
  `perun` again (it used to fall through to a global fact because `perun` is
  registered hidden). A hidden project named by slug from anywhere else resolves
  to nothing: only the owner working inside `perun` can read, run, or store
  against it. Telegram remains chat-ID-gated and `perun` has no project room, so
  remote PerunChat participants cannot reach it either.
* `perun_memory_store` no longer falls back to a **global** fact when the caller
  named a project that does not resolve (a typo, or a denied hidden project); it
  reports "No accessible project" and stores nothing.

### The remaining audit items

* A reattached run no longer seeds from the session transcript (it concatenated
  every earlier turn into this run's answer). The terminal fallback uses only the
  final assistant message, so the result cannot replay history regardless of the
  service's message ordering. `_admission_landed()` heartbeats the run lease.
* A digest that reaches some chats but not others keeps its items queued, records
  which chats it served, and retries only the ones still missing them. A digest
  delivery is recorded without a message id, so **Open** still posts a fresh
  replyable card instead of editing the list.
* `usage()` retries with a 200-message page when the service rejects `limit=1000`,
  instead of losing the snapshot.
* The docs audit waits up to 10 s for the command to start; a queued command is no
  longer recorded as "wrote nothing".
* PerunChat's reply budget is a rate limit anchored on Perun's own replies
  (eight per room per minute): a room it only reads never trips it, and an
  operator message resets it.
* `PATCH /api/settings` stages the in-place re-encryption of an existing secret
  too, so a rejected request no longer leaves the live key encrypted-but-unsaved.
* Documentation: the message-ordering assumption behind the reattach fallback is
  stated where it matters, and the sensitive-subtree audit is documented as
  security-first (OpenCode keeps its own state outside the project).

### Fixes found by auditing this session's own changes

* **Upgrade safety.** A filesystem snapshot written before `parent_dirs` /
  `sensitive` existed no longer turns every sibling directory (or every
  `.opencode` file) into an "escape"/violation: with a legacy snapshot only a
  genuinely new sibling name is reported, and the sensitive comparison is skipped
  until a fresh snapshot exists. Without this, the first execution after the
  upgrade failed with `[POLICY VIOLATION … escape(s)]`.
* **PerunChat retry.** The reconnect loop read `settings.perunchat()` a second
  time *outside* its guard; a bad encrypted secret could still kill the thread.
  It now uses the key/endpoint `_refresh_credentials()` already resolved.
* **No duplicate restart notice.** `runs_awaiting_reply()` no longer includes
  `interrupted` runs: the bridge's `_notify_interrupted_runs()` already announces
  them, and delivering them here too sent two messages for one restart. The
  status is still final, so a waiting worker/stream stops correctly.

### The post-execution docs step has its own restricted agent, and is audited

* `perun-docs` (new, managed like `perun-orchestrator`: write-once with sha256,
  refresh only while untouched, reset on request) is the identity of the session
  that runs `/update-docs`. It may read the project and write `docs/**`,
  `AGENTS.md` and `perun.md`; the blanket deny covers shell and every other tool.
  Before this, the docs run used the project's default agent, so approving two
  source files quietly granted full-tool access to the repository.
* The docs run is now accountable too: Perun snapshots the project before the
  command, waits (bounded, 10 min) for the turn to go idle, diffs, and logs a
  `docs_audit` activity row — `docs_audit_violation` with the paths when a write
  landed outside the docs surface. The proposal's own result is never changed by
  this, and a busy docs slot still writes the changelog bullet as before.
* The global install creates both agents.
